title: A-D-M
hook: adam, adamah (earth), adom (red): the human is earthy

segments.voice: Yesterday, three words for soul: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, and a breath that made a figure alive. Your line was soul is breath. Today, the figure itself, and what it was made of.

A spade goes into a garden bed in spring and turns over a clump of earth: dark, damp, smelling of rain, a worm sliding out of sight. In Hebrew, that clump is adamah. Now look at the person holding the spade. In Hebrew, that's adam. Same three letters, alef, dalet, mem, with one small sound added for the ground. The gardener and the garden share a root. The Torah builds its first human out of the very word for soil, and then keeps playing with the sound.
screen: `A CLUMP OF EARTH: ADAMAH.` → `THE ONE HOLDING IT: ADAM.` → `THE SAME THREE LETTERS.`

segments.voice: A-D-M. Alef, dalet, mem. Turn it four ways. First, adamah, the ground. In Genesis chapter two, God forms the human "of the dust of the ground." Ground there is adamah. Second, the human: ha-adam. The story names its creature after its material, and some readers bring the pun into English as earthling. The next chapter says it out loud: "for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return." Third, adom, red. Further on in Genesis, Esau comes in from the field, faint with hunger, and begs his brother for the red stew on the fire. Then the text adds: "therefore was his name called Edom." Red, Edom: the Torah makes that pun itself. Some readers go one step further and hear red in adam too, the reddish color of clay. Fourth, what the rabbis did with one clay. The Mishnah, in tractate Sanhedrin, asks why the human was created as a single person. One answer it gives: for the sake of peace, so that no one could say to another, my ancestor was greater than yours. Everyone traces back to one figure, and that figure to a handful of ground. Nobody's dust is finer than anyone else's. Not the king's, not yours, not anyone's.
screen: `ADAMAH: THE GROUND.` · `ADAM: NAMED FOR ITS MATERIAL.` · `ADOM: RED, LIKE EDOM'S STEW.` · `ONE CLAY, SO NO ONE OUTRANKS.` · then, large: `אָדָם · אֲדָמָה`

segments.voice: If there's soil nearby, a garden or a plant pot on the sill, put your fingers into it; if not, a stone, a wooden table or the floor under your feet will do. Feel the texture, cool or warm, gritty or smooth, and say the two words one after the other: adamah, adam, ground, human. If you pray, you can give thanks for being made of the earth.
A-D-M. Alef, dalet, mem: adamah, the ground; adam, the human made from it; and adom, red, the color of the clay and Edom's stew. Today's word.
Your line: human from earth. Same ground, so nobody's ancestor outranks anybody's. See you back here tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews read the creation of adam from the adamah in Genesis, and the Mishnah in tractate Sanhedrin teaches from it that humans share one ancestry, so that no one may claim a greater lineage than another.

It's a name meaning the strong one, given because he was made full-grown.
